text:
alex: Heads-up — I'm opening a small PR to trim the long structured-output examples in the Function Calling guide. They duplicate a lot of payload noise and confuse the SDK snippets. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1287 :eyes:
megan: Nice. Is this the prune-for-compact-examples change we discussed in the docs sync? Want to make sure we keep the canonical 'envelope' example somewhere for integrators.
sam: +1 for compact. Suggest we keep one full verbose example in a hidden section and link to it from the compact examples. That way we don't lose the full schema reference.
lina: I skimmed the PR — looks good but there's a broken internal link in the JSON-schema section (line ~42). Also the SDK snippet in the Python quickstart still shows the old `response['result']` shape.
alex: thanks — I fixed the link locally, will push. Which SDK snippet file is that? I can update in the same PR if it's small.
jordan: Python snippet lives in /snippets/python/invoke_examples.md. There's also a JS variant in /snippets/js/invoke_compact.md. Both need updated shapes and a short note about parse fallbacks.
doc-bot: Reminder: please include CHANGELOG entry and mark the PR as docs-only to skip release pipeline.
megan: For the snippet changes, we should show both the compact envelope and the fallback parse code. Something like:
```python
# compact envelope format
resp = client.invoke(... )
data = resp['output']['compact']
# fallback if parser fails
if 'compact' not in resp['output']:
    data = resp['output'].get('raw_text', resp['output'])
```
sam: That fallback example is good. Can we also add a one-liner note on why compact helps (less token noise, better parse heuristics)? Short sentence under the snippet.
lina: Also flag: the example uses `tool_call` field name; our current runtime emits `invocation` for some models. We should normalise examples to show `invocation` with a parenthetical note about `tool_call` legacy name.
alex: ok I'll canonicalise to `invocation` and add: "(legacy SDKs may still emit `tool_call`)"
jordan: FYI ops asked we don't change stable API surfaces in docs without a compatibility note. This is fine as long as we call out both.
megan: Quick doc hygiene: can we add a cross-link from the migration guide (docs/migration/structured-output.md) to the compact example and to the verbose appendix? That will reduce future confusion.
sam: Agreed. Also propose adding a tiny test in the docs CI that ensures every invoke snippet contains either `compact` or `raw_text` so we don't regress.
doc-bot: CI action suggestion posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/actions/runs/987654321
alex: I'll include the link fixes, snippet updates, migration-guide crosslink, changelog note, and the CI test in PR 1287. Requesting reviews from @megan and @lina.
megan: I can review after lunch. If it's small, feel free to merge once I leave an approval. :+1:
lina: I'll run quick grep for any other `tool_call` occurrences and post results here before you merge.
jordan: Heads-up — chatops will pick up the PR title; please avoid slashes and emojis. Keep it descriptive: "docs: compact examples for function invocation + migration links".
alex: good call. I'll rename. Pushing updates now.
megan: Thanks — this should tidy up the Function Calling guide a lot.
sam: Thanks Alex, great cleanup.
lina: posted grep results: found two more `tool_call` mentions in snippets/legacy/*.md — I'll PR a small replace if you want me to.
alex: please do and @megan please watch that PR too. I'll merge mine after your approval and once the link fix is verified.
megan: watching.
doc-bot: PR 1287 updated: link fix pushed, snippets modified, changelog added.
ajson: -- (bot suffix)
